title: Two-beat versus four-beat and tuba versus string bass
summary: Hall says New Orleans bands played two beat, and in New York dance bands used tuba, with Duke Hamilton's an exception.

story.theme_name: Drummers and drumming: who played what, and how
story.community_name: Bass players: lineage, tone and technique

blocks.x: What about, did they use two beat in the old days, a straight four or what, when you first came to New Orleans?
No, they was using two beats. They was using two beats. They was using two beats.
Who do you think introduced four? Or did they ever introduce you there when you were here?

No, they wasn't. Four beat wasn't introduced. Only some drummers would use four beats sometimes, like on the last chorus going out, he would go to four. But everybody was using two beats. Sometimes when you get to that last chorus everybody's shouting, then you'd go to four beats. What about real slow blues?
Did anybody ever play four on that?

No, I don't remember anybody playing four on the slow blues. I'll tell you another thing, when I went to New York everybody was playing tuba in a regular dance band. You know what we were with stuff like stuff stuff like stuff like stuff

they'd use a string bass. I was surprised to see them, but one band I think that I knew that was using a string band, that was Duke Hamilton. Bro happened to be playing that, and he was playing bass violin, but all the rest of the band was playing tubas.
